correctness.rationale: For fair independent separator bits the covariance with their sum is one quarter of the sum of insertion influences. Conditional on the two local lengths, the distinctness gain at size j is the indicator of no unchanged occurrence times the new-child count at j, subtracting a child duplicate and subtracting loss of the parent. A size-j part in an interior region uses the cut–(j−1 noncuts)–cut word of probability 2^{−j−1}. Its distinct starts separated by less than j have incompatible bits; starts j apart share one cut; others are independent. For independent dependency neighborhoods the void estimate used in (3) was also derived directly: for k≥1 set f(k)=∫₀¹t^{k−1}exp(−λt)dt and f(0)=f(1). Integration by parts gives λf(k+1)−kf(k)=1_{k=0}−exp(−λ), and the one-step differences are bounded by f(1)≤min(1,1/λ). Subtracting the sum outside each neighborhood, independent of its indicator, bounds the expected Stein residual by that difference bound times b1+b2. After conditioning on local lengths at most M=ceil(4 log₂ n), remove word positions intersecting conditioned bits or domain endpoints. There are O(j+M) omitted starts. An unchanged word that remains possible among them can use at most one forced endpoint cut: the interior of the affected parent or children cannot be inside another part, and splits at the obligatory ends only cost one endpoint bit. Hence the summed omitted-word probability is O((j+M)2^{−j}), uniformly in the central window. The same envelope covers the mean adjustment and the dependency-neighborhood error. Geometric-run probabilities give the pivotal signed weight (3−j)2^{−j}−4^{−j}; multiplying the void error by its absolute indicator bound costs O(j(j+M)4^{−j}) per cut and size. The sum is o(1) since the window starts at ¾ log₂ n. Truncating local lengths costs O(n(log n)2^{−M}); O(log n) boundary cuts are negligible by the truncated-geometric bound O((j+1)2^{−j}). For small j one can choose Ω(n/(j+1)) disjoint full interior words avoiding the changed bit; any success is unchanged, yielding superpolynomial void suppression. The large-j geometric tail and the central duplicate term are negligible even after summing over cuts. Thus the expression reduces to (1/2)∑(3−j)t_j exp(−t_j) with t_j=n2^{−j−1}, up to absolute o(1). Lattice reindexing and the exponential tails give the asserted A and B including the constant 4 inside B. The Mellin integral gives Γ(1−2πiℓ/ln 2)/ln 2, nonzero at ℓ=1, so positivity, nonconstancy and eventual negative covariance follow; log-moment integration gives the stated period mean for B. Independent finite corroboration used coefficients of (1−y[x/(1−x)−x^j])^{-1} and its y-derivative via a short denominator recurrence, then compared with direct composition enumeration through n=12. For sample n=64,91,128,181,256,362,512,724,1024, exact covariance minus the predicted profile had absolute value at most 4.08×10^{−5}. The infinite result is supplied by the error analysis, not the comparisons.
residual_risks: The expansion is for all positive integers tending to infinity and uniform compositions, not a proof of a finite-size sign threshold or of a uniform expansion for biased cuts.

evidence: Using a multiplicity mark x^r y for r>0 in Hwang–Yeh encodes x^{K_n}y^{D_n}. Bender–Canfield supply limit results for specified local statistics, number of parts, and growth of distinct sizes; Hitczenko–Louchard analyze the marginal distinctness distribution and moments.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The Hwang–Yeh framework covers exact coefficient extraction, which is credited, but does not in the inspected passages give the required uniform derivative/central-size asymptotics. A finite family of fixed-length marks does not cover the growing logarithmic size window or the periodic order-one correction.

evidence: Hitczenko–Stengle obtain E D_n = log₂ n + γ/ln 2 − 1/2 + periodic term + o(1), a marginal mean at uniform sampling. Finch compares K_n to the maximum. The related same-day work derives a maximum covariance and the general influence/derivative relation. Hwang–Yeh's exact marks recover the finite joint distribution.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: One cannot differentiate a fixed-p asymptotic of the marginal mean or its little-o error to get an absolute-o(1) covariance expansion. Nor does a largest-part covariance determine the count of exact occupied lengths. Further uniform asymptotic control of the new statistic is substantive, and its full profile is not supplied by these statements.

evidence: The covariance is p(1−p) times the derivative of E_p[D_n], hence one quarter at p=1/2. The same-day largest-part result uses this method and an agreeing leading lattice profile after an index shift (with its phase log₂(N−1)), but differentiates a different statistic. Largest part tracks exceedance of a threshold; number of distinct sizes counts represented exact lengths.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Allowing equivalent score, derivative, marking and lattice shift formulations does not identify the two statistics. For example with n=6, (3,3) and (3,2,1) have the same maximum and different distinctness. The relevant conditional void probabilities differ (no exact length versus no length above a threshold).

originality.rationale: Prior exact generating functions encode the mixed statistic, and marginal distinctness already exhibits dyadic oscillations. The strongest catalog overlap also studies the same mixed-covariance mechanism with number of parts, but the second variable is maximum part size, not the number of represented part sizes. The distinctness asymptotic through constant order is the supported contribution, not the exact generating function, influence identity, or generic phenomenon of periodicity.
residual_risks: The exact joint function is prior in encoded form; an unlocated joint asymptotic analysis or a sufficiently uniform biased-composition theorem might imply the profile pair. The same-day result for the maximum already contains a closely related leading profile and method; these are not novel in isolation.

value.rationale: The result measures dependence between two natural statistics of the same composition—fragmentation and diversity. It resolves the sign and full logarithmic order, proves that a constant leading coefficient does not suffice, and exhibits the absolute-accuracy second term. These are informative mixed-statistic features not given by the known marginal distinctness behavior or by covariance with the maximum.
residual_risks: No exact sign classification or covariance theorem for general locally restricted compositions is claimed.
